# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required libraries
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git clone)
# libgomp1 is the GNU OpenMP runtime library, a common dependency for parallel codes
# FIX: Added python3 as it is a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake build system
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code into a temporary directory
# A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce image size
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /tmp/lammps-src

# Configure, build, and install LAMMPS from source
# The build is configured to include the required REAXFF package and MPI support
# KSPACE is also included as it's commonly used with FFTW
RUN cd /tmp/lammps-src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
        -D PKG_KSPACE=yes && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a system location on the PATH
# This makes 'lmp' directly available to users and scripts
RUN cp /tmp/lammps-src/build/lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set OpenMPI runtime parameters for better compatibility in containerized environments
# This helps prevent common errors when running MPI applications inside containers
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0 \
    OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0

# Create a final working directory for the application
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the specific example files into the working directory
RUN cp /tmp/lammps-src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Clean up the temporary source code directory to minimize final image size
RUN rm -rf /tmp/lammps-src

# Set the final working directory for the container's entrypoint
WORKDIR /app

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to run a LAMMPS experiment
# on a single Kubernetes node, suitable for a CPU-based instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # The namespace to deploy to
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to ensure all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # The LAMMPS command uses -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2, indicating a 2x2x2 decomposition,
  # which corresponds to 8 total MPI ranks (2*2*2=8).
  tasks: 8

  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any error and print verbose output.
    strict: true

  # Defines the containers that will run as part of the MiniCluster.
  # Only one container is specified, as required.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator will wrap this
      # command with `flux run -n <tasks> ...`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      
      # This container is a worker, not the one that submits the job.
      # This MUST be false for worker pods.
      launcher: false
      
      # This container should have the Flux broker and workers running inside.
      runFlux: true

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest is configured to run a LAMMPS experiment
# on a single AWS Graviton (ARM) Kubernetes node.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # The namespace to deploy to
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to ensure all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # The LAMMPS command uses -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2, indicating a 2x2x2 decomposition,
  # which corresponds to 8 total MPI ranks (2*2*2=8).
  tasks: 8

  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator
  logging:
    # Fail on any error and print verbose output.
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications for the MiniCluster pods
  pod:
    # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure sufficient resources.
    # The t4g.2xlarge instance has 8 vCPUs, matching the 8 tasks required,
    # resolving the "unsatisfiable request" error from the previous attempt.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: t4g.2xlarge

  # Flux-specific settings
  flux:
    # Specifies the architecture for the flux-view sidecar.
    # This is required for ARM-based nodes like AWS Graviton (t4g.*).
    arch: arm

    # Defines the container image for the flux-view sidecar.
    container:
      # Overrides the default flux-view image to use an ARM-compatible version.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the main application container for the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator will wrap this
      # command with `flux run -n <tasks> ...`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      
      # This container is a worker, not the one that submits the job.
      # This MUST be false for worker pods.
      launcher: false
      
      # This container should have the Flux broker and workers running inside.
      runFlux: true

# This manifest corrects the previous scheduling failure by specifying a valid
# high-performance AWS instance type and scales the job to fully utilize it.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size is 1, ensuring the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # Updated to 64 tasks to fully utilize the vCPUs on the m7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Keep pods after completion for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging for detailed error reporting.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # m7g instances are ARM-based, so the architecture must be set to 'arm'.
    arch: arm
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image, required for Graviton instances.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod-level specifications for the MiniCluster pods.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Corrected to a valid AWS instance type. The m7g.16xlarge has 64 CPUs
      # and 256 GiB of memory, matching the resource requirements for this run.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Defines the main application container.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    # Updated command for the full-scale optimization run. The previous command
    # with x/y/z values of 2, 2, 2 resulted in 8 tasks. This command is not
    # directly related to the task count, but is part of the new experiment run.
    command: lmp -v x 16 -v y 16 -v z 16 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    # This is a worker container, not the job launcher. Must be false.
    launcher: false
    # The Flux runtime environment will be started in this container.
    runFlux: true

# This manifest corrects the "FailedScheduling" error by specifying a valid AWS
# instance type in the nodeSelector. The previous type, "hpc-instance-64core-256gb",
# did not exist, preventing the pod from being scheduled. The fix replaces it with
# "m7g.16xlarge", a 64-core ARM instance, aligning with the job's requirements.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size is 1, ensuring the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The number of tasks for this optimization run.
  tasks: 16

  # Keep pods after completion for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging for detailed error reporting.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # m7g instances are ARM-based, so the architecture must be set to 'arm'.
    arch: arm
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image, required for Graviton instances.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod-level specifications for the MiniCluster pods.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Corrected to a valid AWS instance type. m7g.16xlarge has 64 CPUs
      # and 256 GiB of memory, matching the resource target for this run.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Defines the main application container.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    command: lmp -v x 16 -v y 16 -v z 16 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    # This is a worker container, not the job launcher. Must be false.
    launcher: false
    # The Flux runtime environment will be started in this container.
    runFlux: true

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_lammps_run(
    total_atoms: int,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_performance: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_perf_per_core: float = 150000.0,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 40000.0,
    atoms_per_gb: float = 1.5e6,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Evaluates a LAMMPS run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.

    This function acts as a "diagnostician" by analyzing the performance of a
    completed LAMMPS run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most
    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and
    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.

    Args:
        total_atoms (int): The total number of atoms in the simulation.
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_performance (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in timesteps/second.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).
        ideal_perf_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max performance of a single core (default 150,000 timesteps/sec).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for atoms/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 40,000).
        atoms_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (atoms per GB of RAM, default 1.5e6).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero.", "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS"}

    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    atoms_per_rank = total_atoms / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node
    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank
    
    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(atoms_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_perf_per_core = ideal_perf_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_perf = effective_perf_per_core * total_cores_used

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_perf > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_performance / theoretical_max_perf

    estimated_memory_gb = total_atoms / atoms_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0
    
    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "atoms_per_rank": int(atoms_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_perf_timesteps_sec": f"{theoretical_max_perf:.2e}"
    }

    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---
    
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of atoms is too large for the allocated memory.",
            "strategy_hint": "DECREASE_ATOMS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of atoms per rank is too small (communication-bound).",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ATOMS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.",
        "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ATOMS",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
